2 ترّحهُ , (S, A, K,) inf. n. تَتْرِيحٌ; (S, K;) and ↓ اترحهُ ; (A, Msb;) It (an affair, or an event, &c., TA,) grieved him; it made him sorrowful, unhappy, or anxious. (S, A, Msb, K.) A poet cited by IAar says, “قَد طَالَ مَا تَرَّحَهَا المُتَرِّحُ
” [Long did that which made unhappy make her, or them, unhappy]; meaning that the pasturage rendered troublesome her, or their, state. (Th, AZ, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
